content.comment_body: Hello everyone, apologies for the basic question. I'm encountering conflicting information about the [product_name] 24rc model, article number [article_no]. Does this variant offer high-speed inputs on I3, I4, I5, and I6? I've come across technical documents claiming none of the [article_no] versions have high-speed inputs, others saying all of them do, and a knowledgeable post here states the AC/DC 24RC version doesn't support high-speed inputs. Which statement is accurate?
Hi, your [product_name] does not feature high-speed inputs. That function is only present on the DC version of the [product_name]. Hope this clarifies things.

Thanks for confirming. Is there a manual specifically for this model? I've only been able to find documentation that covers several models together. Choosing the right version is tougher than expected, as each model offers different functions. My project involves logging values from a speed sensor (Hall-effect type) and a temperature sensor (PT100). I have already ordered an RTD module and use a power supply from [company_name]. Which [product_name] would be most appropriate? It would be helpful if the module included a display, and I intend to switch a 240V supply as well.

Hello, since you need high-speed inputs, you should consider the [article_no] [product_name] 24C, or the [article_no] [product_name] 12/24RC — both offer 8 digital inputs (4 analog inputs)/4 digital outputs, with a 200 block limit. Note: The first model requires external relays for 230V outputs, while the second can handle resistive loads up to 10A with built-in relays. Generally, using external relays to switch large loads is best for easier replacement if a relay fails. If you need more than 200 blocks, opt for the [version_no] range. See further details at [url]. Regards, [user_name]
Thank you, [user_name]. I have placed an order for the 12/24RC model.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report challenges identifying which [product_name] variants provide high-speed input features. Conflicting technical resources and unclear naming conventions add confusion, especially when specific hardware details are crucial for their projects. There is a clear demand for simplified and more robust technical documentation as well as clearer distinctions between different models.
analysis.user_expectations: Users look for straightforward and clear documentation regarding model functionalities, specifically about high-speed input options. They expect practical advice on the optimal [product_name] to select for specialized tasks such as sensor data logging and built-in display integration.
